mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals supply-side disruptions, which typically lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as production slowdowns impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as cheap borrowing costs fuel investment and consumption.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% and PAYEMS falls > 100k in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of increasing housing starts (HOUST) and rising real GDP (GDPC1) signals strengthening demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and GDPC1 increases > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4%) during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) signals a misaligned monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the real cost of borrowing increases without corresponding inflationary pressure.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
